summary.headline: v1.0.1 fixes Android auth race, signOut, and iOS offlineAccess. Core risk remains JS-trusted OAuth config with new Android parity gaps in requestScopes/revokeAccess.

findings.title: Unpinned webClientId enables OAuth client redirection
findings.attackScenario: Compromised in-app JS calls configure({ webClientId: attackerClient, offlineAccess: true }) before sign-in; user completes Google UI; idToken and serverAuthCode issued for attacker's OAuth client.
findings.impact: OAuth token phishing; serverAuthCode exchange on attacker backend; PII in idToken
findings.recommendation: Pin webClientId at build time; call configure once from trusted code; document JS trust model

findings.title: configure() re-callability enables mid-session OAuth client hijack
findings.attackScenario: Legitimate configure() at startup; malicious JS re-calls configure() with attacker webClientId after sign-in; subsequent requestScopes/getTokens use attacker client while cached idToken may reflect prior client.
findings.impact: Mid-session OAuth client redirection; mixed client binding between cached idToken and new serverAuthCode
findings.recommendation: Enforce configure-once in native release builds; reject or ignore subsequent configure() calls

findings.title: Unrestricted OAuth scope escalation via requestScopes/configure.scopes
findings.attackScenario: Malicious JS requests sensitive Google API scopes; user approves consent; serverAuthCode returned to JS and scopes persisted on Android.
prerequisites: Active Google session or Android authorize without session guard
findings.impact: Elevated Google API access via exchanged serverAuthCode
findings.recommendation: Consumer allowlist scopes; optional native allowedScopes config

findings.title: Android requestScopes() lacks signed-in session guard
findings.attackScenario: Malicious JS calls configure() then requestScopes([SENSITIVE]) before app sign-in flow; authorization UI may appear; serverAuthCode returned without sign-in success callback.
findings.impact: Scope authorization bypassing app sign-in flow on Android; iOS has equivalent guard
findings.recommendation: Require getLastSignedInUserId() or equivalent before requestScopes on Android

findings.title: Silent token retrieval via signIn() and getTokens()
findings.attackScenario: After one sign-in, compromised JS calls signIn() (iOS) or getTokens() (Android) without user interaction and exfiltrates idToken and accessToken.
findings.impact: Silent bearer token retrieval; no fresh user challenge
findings.recommendation: Document silent restore semantics; treat post-sign-in token APIs as sensitive

findings.title: Android revokeAccess() always forces logout regardless of target or success
findings.attackScenario: Malicious JS calls revokeAccess('arbitrary@gmail.com'); finally block always runs signOut() and clears Credential Manager state even when revoke fails.
findings.recommendation: Validate emailOrUniqueId matches active session; do not unconditionally signOut in finally

findings.title: Auto-generated nonce not returned for backend OIDC verification
findings.attackScenario: Backend enforces nonce claim verification but app uses default auto-nonce; verification impossible without skipping checks.
findings.impact: Broken or skipped nonce validation; weakened replay protection
findings.recommendation: Return nonce to JS or require explicit configure({ nonce }) with documented verification flow

findings.title: JWT payload parsed without signature verification (claims fallback)
findings.attackScenario: Forged credential reaching parseCredential would trust unverified JWT claims for sub/email fallback.
findings.recommendation: Rely on SDK fields only; remove JWT parse fallback if redundant

findings.title: GoogleSignInError class not constructed from native exceptions
findings.attackScenario: Apps using instanceof GoogleSignInError fail; isErrorWithCode() still works for bridged errors.
findings.impact: Error handling bugs; possible SDK message leakage in logs
findings.recommendation: Map native exceptions to GoogleSignInError in JS wrapper

findings.title: iOS custom URL scheme hijacking (platform limitation)
findings.attackScenario: Malicious app registers same REVERSED_CLIENT_ID scheme; intercepts OAuth redirect.
prerequisites: User completes OAuth in victim app
findings.recommendation: Document platform risk; consider Universal Links where supported

findings.title: Android clearCachedAccessToken() missing token ownership check
findings.attackScenario: Attacker with leaked access token calls clearCachedAccessToken(leakedToken); Android clears token without verifying current session ownership.
prerequisites: Compromised JS or attacker with token
findings.impact: Token invalidation DoS; no token theft
findings.recommendation: Mirror iOS validation — reject tokens not matching current user session

findings.title: Unpinned @expo/config-plugins runtime dependency in published package
findings.attackScenario: Compromised future @expo/config-plugins version resolved on consumer install affects Expo prebuild on developer machines via internal import path.
findings.impact: Build-time supply chain risk for Expo consumers; unused dep in bare RN apps
findings.recommendation: Pin version range; move to optional peer dependency; avoid internal /build/ imports

positives: Android AES-GCM encrypted token storage with Android Keystore
Authorization mutex prevents concurrent auth race (RNGS-003 fixed)
iOS token ownership checks on clearCachedAccessToken and revokeAccess
